scope: Different-author, static-only hammer review of the exact M1910 signal-safe clean-environment two-axis C2 fast-min hold-repair runner. The review accepted the explicitly supplied trust model: a runner cannot hash-pin itself, and the launch trust root is the user's direct invocation of the separately authored, separately reviewed release/audit chain with four exact SHA-256 arguments. It therefore did not fail M1910 merely because those four digests are positional arguments. It rechecked exact source and predecessor pins, upstream double seals, two-axis fairness, one-shot namespace ordering, signal terminality, lock ownership, clean tool environments, two-call cardinality, setup/hold/DRC/area gates, canonical publication postconditions, claim boundaries and docs/359 identity. No license query, attempt, Design Compiler, VCS, PrimeTime, Formality, PTPX, result publication, runner/Tcl/predecessor mutation or docs/359 mutation was performed.
verdict: FAIL CLOSED. M1910 correctly fixes M1901's rc=0 signal defect by forcing INT/TERM/HUP to 130/143/129, and its ordinary active failure path seals and publishes a fixed no-retry quarantine. It also preserves the exact frozen K8 and equal-bandwidth K1x8 inputs, one license query after attempt consumption, exactly two DC calls, the 3.000/0.200 ns setup contract, 0.070 ns hold-optimization guard restored to 0.050 ns reporting, per-axis 5 percent area ceilings, setup/hold zero-violation gates, five design-rule zero-violation sections and raw no-PT/no-Formality/no-power claim boundary. Launch remains forbidden because the cleanup handler removes the shared lock even when this process never acquired it, and because ACTIVE is armed only after WORK creation, leaving a signal/failure window that can strand an unsealed WORK directory without a terminal quarantine. The future review/audit semantic parser also omits exact review/audit schema, milestone and reviewer identity checks; this is non-blocking by itself under the stated external SHA trust root, but should be tightened in the successor. No M1912 release, license query, attempt or DC is authorized.

trust_model.limitation: The parser does not require exact review/audit schema, milestone or reviewer_identity; see M1911-P2-01. Under the stated external exact-SHA launch root this is metadata hardening, not an independent authority bypass.

findings.finding: The EXIT/signal cleanup removes the shared launch lock without proving that this process acquired it.
findings.evidence: LOCK is a fixed shared path at line 41. The traps are installed at lines 58-61 before any lock acquisition, while finish unconditionally executes rmdir LOCK at line 55. LOCK has no LOCK_HELD/ownership flag. Therefore a second instance that exits at the freshness gate on line 98 because the first instance's empty LOCK exists invokes finish and can remove the first instance's lock. The same cross-process deletion is possible on any earlier validation failure while another owner holds the empty lock.
findings.impact: The one-shot mutual-exclusion invariant can be destroyed by an unauthorized or simply concurrent losing invocation. A later process can then pass the lock gate while the original two-DC campaign is active, permitting duplicate tool use and namespace races.
findings.required_fix: Introduce LOCK_HELD=0; set it to 1 only after this process's atomic mkdir LOCK succeeds; in finish and the success path remove LOCK only when LOCK_HELD=1, then clear it. Never remove a lock that this process did not acquire.

findings.finding: WORK can be created while failure quarantine handling is still disarmed.
findings.evidence: Line 111 executes mkdir LOCK, then mkdir WORK, then ACTIVE=1. If mkdir WORK succeeds and a signal is delivered before the following shell assignment, or if the shell fails at that boundary, finish sees ACTIVE=0 and skips lines 51-54. It then removes the lock. The fresh unsealed WORK directory remains, with no ATTEMPT, RESULT or FAILURE terminal evidence.
findings.impact: The successor fixes the prior signal exit code but still has a partial-attempt namespace mutation that is not terminally sealed. Manual deletion would be required before any relaunch, and the failure chain would not prove whether external tool access occurred.
findings.required_fix: After acquiring the owned lock, arm ACTIVE before creating WORK (for example LOCK_HELD=1; ACTIVE=1; mkdir WORK). The failure handler already checks that WORK exists, so an ACTIVE=1 state before mkdir is safe and ensures every successfully created WORK directory is quarantined on nonzero exit.

findings.finding: The future review and audit semantic checks omit exact schema, milestone and reviewer identity fields.
findings.evidence: Lines 84-86 require only review status, zero counts and runner SHA. Lines 93-95 require only audit status, zero counts and the three-field chain identity. The release itself is checked much more strictly, including schema and exact dictionaries.
findings.impact: Under the accepted external exact-SHA trust root this does not permit substitution by itself, but it makes the runtime semantic proof weaker than the separately reviewed artifacts and leaves different-author separation implicit.
findings.required_fix: In the successor require exact M1915 review schema/milestone/reviewer_identity and exact M1917 audit schema/milestone/reviewer_identity, in addition to the current status/count/identity checks and double seals.
